label: Electricity price, flat
source: ElCom 2026, Basel (BFS 2701), IWB, category H4, total, excl. VAT
note: Queried from the ElCom interface; the raw answer is kept with the project files. ElCom figures exclude VAT; the case asks for the 2026 price although the weather year is 2025. Both alternatives are shown as sensitivities.

label: Electricity price with 8.1 % VAT (sensitivity)
source: Recombined from the IWB 2026 tariff sheet: VAT applies to energy, grid use and federal levies, not to the two Basel levies
note: The same method reproduces IWB's published prices with VAT. What a private household pays.

label: Electricity price of 2025, the simulated weather year (sensitivity)
source: ElCom 2025, Basel (BFS 2701), IWB, category H4, total, excl. VAT

label: Efficiency of the heat pump that server heat replaces
source: Case brief (value of the heat = electricity price / 2.5)
note: Swiss field monitoring found 3.4 on average for air-to-water units; shown as a sensitivity.

label: Efficiency of air-to-water heat pumps measured in Swiss homes (sensitivity)
source: Swiss Federal Office of Energy, field monitoring of heat pumps, heating season 2022/23: air-to-water units
note: With this value the heat the servers replace is worth less than the case's COP 2.5 assumes. For hot-water charging the same units averaged 2.9, so for this house's mix of heating and hot water about 3.3.

label: Price of contracted batch work (modern 1 kW server)
source: Team estimate between market anchors (range 0.70 to 1.80). The anchors are for 192 processor threads, taken as about 1 kW of servers: rented as two dedicated Hetzner AX162 that is CHF 0.81 an hour at the monthly cap and about CHF 1.82 billed by the hour, plus a setup fee of EUR 304 per server; cloud spot capacity costs CHF 2.00 to 2.44 an hour (AWS)
note: A judgement, not a quoted price. A single basement host without a service agreement can hardly charge more than a data-centre provider's hourly rate. Whether a buyer contracts such a host at all is a separate question the model does not answer. 1 kW of the new servers on the Money page has about 300 threads; the price is not scaled up for that, so it leans low.

label: Price of interruptible filler work (modern 1 kW server)
source: Team estimate, on the cautious side (range 0.30 to 0.90). Anchors, for 192 processor threads taken as about 1 kW: marketplace prices a renter pays for interruptible capacity, CHF 0.81 for processors only and CHF 1.13 with memory (Salad), and an asking price of CHF 0.71 (Akash)
note: What hosts are paid on such marketplaces is not published and can be zero. 1 kW of the new servers on the Money page has about 300 threads; the price is not scaled up for that, so it leans low.

label: Contracted batch jobs arriving per day and house
source: Team assumption, no market source. Chosen so that contracted work (about 12 server-hours a day) fits the summer heat budget of 15 server-hours a day
note: Missed deadlines rise steeply with this number; the Jobs page shows 3, 6, 12 and 24 jobs a day.

label: Job rates shown as a comparison on the Jobs page
source: Team choice

label: How contracted jobs arrive
value: random (Poisson), the same rate every hour of the day and every day of the year
source: Team assumption, no market source
note: No daily or seasonal pattern in demand for contracted work.

label: Completion window of a contracted job
source: Product shape of commercial batch interfaces that promise completion within 24 hours; no source from a market for processor batch work
note: Work delivered inside the window is paid; the rest is cancelled and the job counts as missed. 12 and 48 hours are shown as sensitivities.

label: Median size of a contracted job
source: Alibaba PAI GPU trace 2020, median instance run-time 23 min (NSDI 2022, section 3.2)
note: The trace's run-times are taken directly as server-hours on a 1 kW server. That mapping from a GPU cluster to processor work is the team's assumption.

label: 90th percentile of the job size
source: Alibaba PAI GPU trace 2020, P90 instance run-time 4.5 h (NSDI 2022, section 3.2)
note: Sizes follow a lognormal curve through the median and the 90th percentile. Above the 90th percentile the curve is an extrapolation (95th percentile 9.0, 99th 33.5 server-hours).

label: Largest contracted job
source: Team assumption
note: Two servers for a full window. The largest jobs cause most missed deadlines; 24 server-hours is shown as a sensitivity.

label: A contracted job can be split across servers and paused at any hour
source: Team assumption
note: A job of 48 server-hours may use all 8 servers in the same hour. Switching a server on or off costs no time and no work; a real cold start takes about 4 minutes (2.5 to 8).

label: Mix of contracted job types
source: Team assumption
note: Labels only: no figure on the dashboard depends on it.

label: Photo indexing job, how it is cut into pieces (CLIP ViT-B/32 vectors of open-licence Memobase photos)
source: Team design
note: Input is 1,904 photos from 12 institutions (public domain, CC0, CC BY and CC BY-SA only). Measured speed and energy are on the Jobs page. The job drives the live demo; it is not part of the contracted-job mix of the yearly model.

label: Interruptible filler work
source: Case brief allows unlimited jobs if stated
note: Filler has no deadline and buys every server-hour the house can use as heat.

label: Random seeds for the job arrivals
source: Team choice
note: Missed deadlines are reported as the mean and the range over the seeds.

label: Reference scheduling policy
source: Team design
note: Keeps only the heat reserve the forecast asks for, so the tank has room for deadline work.

label: Deadline work may run even when its heat has to be dumped
source: Team design, heat comes first
note: With false, a contracted job that is due waits when house and tank are full, and may miss its deadline. Every missed deadline of the reference comes from this rule. The opposite choice is shown on the Method page.

label: Weather forecast used by the scheduler
source: Open-Meteo Previous Runs API (forecasts issued 1 to 7 days ahead in 2025); the mean error of the last 14 days is removed and the forecast is made colder by the safety margin below
note: The one-day-ahead error of +1.1 K is mostly an offset between the forecast's and the archive's grid cell; the calibration removes it. The first 14 days of the year use the errors of late December (the year is treated as a cycle). Perfect foresight is shown as a sensitivity.

label: Forecast horizon
source: Team design
note: A two-day horizon is shown as a sensitivity: the 35 kWh tank, not the forecast, limits how much reserve can be held.

label: Days of past forecast error used to calibrate the forecast
source: Team design

label: Cold-side safety margin of the forecast, in standard errors
source: Team design, chosen from the forecast experiment
note: The reserve is planned against a forecast made colder by this many standard errors of the last 14 days.

label: Safety margin on top of the forecast heat reserve
source: Team design, chosen from the forecast experiment

label: Power drawn by a paused server
source: Paused servers are switched off
note: A plugged-in server in soft-off still draws 8 to 30 W. Servers left idling draw about 145 to 180 W per kW of servers: published idle power is 125 W for 2x EPYC 9654 and 54.8 W for a lightly equipped 2x Xeon Gold 6252, scaled to 1 kW, and fuller memory and drives add more. Both are shown as sensitivities. Start-up time (about 4 minutes) is not modelled.

label: New current-generation 2-socket server (2x EPYC 9554, 384 GB, NVMe)
unit: CHF per server, incl. 8.1 % Swiss import VAT
source: Thomas-Krenn configurator prices, summed from the option lines, plus 8.1 % import VAT (range 18,600 to 34,800)
note: Not a checked-out cart: whether the vendor's prices already include German VAT could not be confirmed (if they do, the price is about CHF 28,400), and the processor option may be a promotion. Memory is 62 % of the price; the low end of the range is a 128 GB build. The 12 memory modules fill half of the 24 memory channels.

label: Depreciation life, new server
source: Annual reports of large cloud operators (Amazon 5 to 6 years, Meta 5.5, Alphabet 6) and Swiss tax practice for data-processing equipment

label: Refurbished previous-generation 2-socket server (2x Xeon Gold 6138, 384 GB)
unit: CHF per server, landed in Switzerland
source: servershop24 and TechMikeNY prices for a build with 12 memory modules of 32 GB, plus 8.1 % import VAT and shipping (range 3,700 to 5,800)
note: Base units were out of stock on the day read; shipping of about CHF 130 is assumed.

label: Full-load wall power, refurbished server
source: Estimate for 2x Xeon Gold 6138 with 384 GB (range 330 to 520), anchored on a SPECpower result of 342 W for the similar 2x Xeon Gold 6252
note: 1 kW of servers therefore needs 1000 / 380 = 2.63 refurbished servers.

label: Depreciation life, refurbished server
source: No published source. Parts from 2017 to 2020 are already 6 to 9 years old and sellers give one year of warranty (range 2 to 4)

label: Work per kWh of a refurbished server, relative to a new one
source: Team estimate from published SPECrate 2017 integer results: 189 for 2x Xeon Gold 6138 and about 1,330 for 2x EPYC 9554. Per kW of the full-load power used here (380 W and 850 W) that is about 500 and 1,560, a ratio of 0.32 (range 0.30 to 0.38)
note: Refurbished server-hours are priced at this share of the new-server prices. The EPYC result was read once and not re-checked.

label: Processor threads of a refurbished server
source: Intel product data, Xeon Gold 6138 (20 cores and 40 threads each, two processors)
note: Used only for the case in which filler work is paid per thread whatever its speed.

label: Processor threads the price anchors refer to
source: The rented and spot offers behind the compute prices (two Hetzner AX162, AWS c7i.48xlarge)
note: Taken as about 1 kW of servers.

label: Interest rate for annualising hardware cost
source: Team assumption without a market source, chosen as a cautious rate for a private investment
note: The yearly cost is the annuity for this rate over the hardware's life. Not included: network connection, maintenance and spare parts, the liquid-cooling fittings that bring server heat into the water loop, marketplace fees, insurance, space and noise.

label: Full-load wall power, new server
source: Engineering estimate (range 700 to 1,000). The two processors alone are rated 720 W; memory, drives, fans and power-supply losses come on top. Published SPECpower results of 720 to 770 W use a lighter load
note: Not measured. 1 kW of servers therefore needs 1000 / 850 = 1.18 new servers. Also used to turn the server's computing speed into work per kWh on the Jobs page.

label: Processor cores of the new server
source: AMD product page, EPYC 9554 (64 cores each, two processors)

label: Clock rate used for the new server's peak computing speed
source: AMD product page, EPYC 9554 (base clock; the all-core boost of 3.75 GHz is defined for light load)

label: Single-precision operations per core and clock cycle, new server
source: AMD (Zen 4 does 16 double-precision operations per cycle; single precision doubles that)
note: 128 cores × 32 × 3.1 GHz = 12.7 trillion operations a second at best.

label: How well a job uses the server's computing speed, relative to the laptop
source: Team assumption, not measured on a server
note: More likely lower than higher on a server with 128 cores; the Jobs page also shows half of it.
